newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt trims losses,lifted by U.S. assets bounce.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt trims losses,lifted by U.S. assets bounce.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices staged a mild recovery Monday afternoon, as U.S. stocks rallied, traders said.
Latin debt prices turned lightly mixed, but East European debts remained depressed. Spreads for Bulgarian Bradys widened some 25 basis points, they said.
The gyraption of U.S. equities, since Dow Index's 247 points, or 3.1 percent drop on Friday, however, continued to unnerve emerging market players, they added.

The stunningly strong 8.8 percent growth of Mexican gross domestic product in the second quarter vindicated the bullish forecasts by many Latin American economists, but the sentiment was tempered by the murder of the brother of Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz.

"The market is focusing more on the macroeconomic picture," said Walter Molano, senior Latin America economist at SBC/Warburg. "We don't have enough facts to make an informed judgment (on the murder)," Alejandro Ortiz was gunned down in Mexico City on Saturday. Police immediately said the crime was a robbery attempt.

To be sure, Molano expected the Mexican economy to "peak out" as the pace of consumer spending, investment boom and export growth that underpinned the economy in the first half, slows down in the second half.

Arturo Porzecanski, chief Latin America economist at ING Barings, agreed that the Mexican growth rate was unsustainable at the current neck-breaking rate, but even a slow-down to a five percent annual growth rate would not be disappointing to investors, he said, adding: "The momentum is very strong."

Brazil reported its current account deficit, which reached $33.45 billion, or 4.35 prcent of GDP in the 12 months to July. But the data did not raise much concern, because Brazil's massive privatization program would continue attractiving foreign capital flows, Porzecanski said.

Traders noted that debt prices of the four major Latin economies -- Mexico, Brazil, Argentina and Venezuela -- were holding well, while the more speculative grades of Ecuador, Panama were showing strains.
Panama IRB and Panama PDI were each off 3/8 at 77-1/8 and 87-1/8. Ecuador Bradys trimmed early losses, with PDI bond edging up 1/8 on the day at 70-1/2.
Compared to Latin debt, Bulgaria and Russian papers failed to recoup much lost ground. The decline was attributed to profit-taking after the spectacular gains early in the year.
As of Friday, August 15, the value of Bulgarian debt rose 58.59 percent year-to-date, while Russian papers appreciated 14.93 percent, according to J.P. Morgan Emerging Markets Index.
Bulgaria FLRB lost 1-1/8 at 62-1/8 and Russia's dollar Vnesh was off 7/8 to 100-3/4.
A trader noted Bulgaria's austerity plan in the structural reform began to exact a price on the economy, which apparently drove some U.S. investors to seek value elsewhere.
